# bdate

> The date and time the way a Byzantine would have reckoned it: the Julian calendar date, the Anno Mundi year (counted from 1 September 5509 BC), the 15-year indiction, Greek weekday and month names, and seasonal (unequal) hours with night watches. bdate.app is a live clock; the same reckoning is available as a JSON web API, a Python command-line tool and a JavaScript library.

Sunrise and sunset, which set the seasonal hours, are approximate (within a few minutes). Dates given as input are read as Gregorian.

## Clock

- [Live clock](https://bdate.app/): the current Byzantine hour for a chosen place; installable and works offline. Query options: `place=athens` (or another preset), `lat=…&lon=…`, `theme=light|dark`, `compact=1` for an embeddable dial alone, `lang=el` for Greek.

## API

- [GET /api/v1/date](https://bdate.app/api/v1/date): returns the reckoning as JSON (`gregorian`, `julian_year`, `julian_month`, `julian_day`, `month_name`, `weekday`, `anno_mundi`, `indiction`, `seasonal`), plus `text` (one-line form) and the `lat`/`lon` used. Optional parameters: `date` (ISO-8601, Gregorian; default now), `tz` (IANA time zone), `lat`, `lon` (default Constantinople), `hours=0` to skip the seasonal hour. Example: https://bdate.app/api/v1/date?date=1453-05-29T05:30&tz=Europe/Istanbul

## Docs

- [Overview](https://bdate.app/docs/): what bdate prints and why
- [Usage](https://bdate.app/docs/usage.html): command-line options, JSON fields, the web API and the JavaScript port
- [The Julian calendar](https://bdate.app/docs/calendar.html): leap years, drift from the Gregorian calendar, conversion
- [Anno Mundi](https://bdate.app/docs/anno-mundi.html): the Byzantine world era and its September new year
- [The indiction](https://bdate.app/docs/indiction.html): the 15-year cycle used to date documents
- [Days and months](https://bdate.app/docs/names.html): the Greek weekday and month names
- [Seasonal hours](https://bdate.app/docs/hours.html): unequal hours and the four night watches
- [Ελληνικά](https://bdate.app/docs/el/): the same pages in Greek

## Source

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/thekyria/bdate): Python reference implementation, JavaScript port, clock and API (MIT licensed)
